tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Guild is: a Claude Code plugin that turns a single `/guild "<task>"` invocation into a self-evolving team of specialist agents. It introduces the lifecycle spine (brainstorm → compose → plan → context → execute → review → verify → reflect) and the headline counts — 14 specialists, 77 skills across 5 tiers, 8 commands, 10 hook events. This page is the roadmap for everything the tour covers next.

tour.title: The Authoritative Architecture
tour.description: guild-plan.md is the single source of truth — every other file in the project is an implementation of a section in this document. It defines the planning contract (§8.1), the wiki and decisions model (§10), the evolve/rollback pipeline (§11), and the command surface (§13.1). Read this to see the design intent before seeing how each piece is wired; CLAUDE.md is the companion that tells Claude itself how to operate inside this repo.

tour.title: Plugin Manifests
tour.description: These manifests are how Claude Code discovers and loads Guild. plugin.json declares the plugin's skills, agents, commands, and hooks; marketplace.json registers it for distribution; .mcp.json wires the two optional stdio MCP servers. Building on the architecture from Step 2, this is the concrete entry point that makes the lifecycle reachable from a user's Claude Code session.
tour.languageLesson: Claude Code plugins are declared entirely in JSON manifests — there is no code entry point. The manifest's relative paths to skills/, agents/, commands/, and hooks/ are the contract the runtime resolves at load time.

tour.title: The Lifecycle Spine (Meta Skills)
tour.description: The meta-skill tier implements the lifecycle the README promised. brainstorm/SKILL.md runs the Socratic flow that captures the §8.1 planning contract into a spec; context-assemble/SKILL.md builds the 3-layer per-specialist context bundle; audit/SKILL.md provides the security gate over installed scripts. Each skill is a SKILL.md definition paired with an evals.json that gates its own evolution — this is the unit Guild improves over time.
tour.languageLesson: Guild skills are Markdown with YAML frontmatter (the SKILL.md convention). The frontmatter `description` carries the trigger contract; the body carries the procedure. Every skill ships a paired evals.json so the evolve loop can score candidate edits.

tour.title: Shipping Specialist Agents
tour.description: The agents/ tree holds the 14 domain specialists the lifecycle dispatches as subagents — architect, backend, frontend, qa, security, devops, mobile, plus the content and commercial roles (copywriter, technical-writer, researcher, marketing, seo, social-media, sales). Building on the context bundle from Step 4, each agent definition is the role guild:execute-plan invokes per lane. They are the workforce; the skills are the playbooks they run.

tour.title: Dev-Team Authoring Scaffolds
tour.description: Separate from the shipping specialists, the .claude/agents/ tree holds the 8 build-time agents that author the plugin itself — plugin-architect, skill-author, command-builder, hook-engineer, tooling-engineer, and others. The _shared/ contracts (handoff-contract, plan-anchors, AUDIT) are the conventions every authoring agent obeys. This is the meta-layer: the team that builds the team.

tour.title: User-Facing Slash Commands
tour.description: The commands/ definitions are the actual entry points users type. guild.md drives the full lifecycle; guild-team, guild-evolve, guild-rollback, guild-wiki, guild-stats, and guild-audit expose the individual operations from guild-plan.md §13.1. Building on the skills (Step 4) and agents (Step 5), these commands are the thin user-facing surface that orchestrates everything underneath.

tour.title: Lifecycle Hooks
tour.description: hooks.json wires native Claude Code hook events to scripts that run automatically. capture-telemetry.ts records run events for the telemetry MCP; maybe-reflect.ts is the Stop-hook gate that triggers guild:reflect when the heuristic clears; bootstrap.sh prepares the environment. This is how Guild gets its self-evolving behavior without the user asking — reflection and gating fire as side effects of normal work.
tour.languageLesson: Claude Code hooks are event-driven: hooks.json maps events (SessionStart, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, …) to executables. The hook receives a JSON event on stdin and signals decisions via exit code and stdout — see the fixtures/ files for the exact event shapes.

tour.title: The Agent-Team Launcher & Hooks
tour.description: The opt-in tmux agent-team backend lets specialists run as parallel teammates instead of sequential subagents. agent-team-launcher.ts spins up the tmux session; the agent-team/ hooks (task-created, task-completed, teammate-idle) coordinate the lifecycle across panes. This is the alternative execution backend referenced in the README's 'opt-in tmux agent-team launcher'.

tour.title: The Evolve & Telemetry Tooling
tour.description: The scripts/ tree is the engine behind Guild's self-improvement claim. evolve-loop.ts runs the §11.2 paired-subagent pipeline; shadow-mode.ts validates a candidate skill silently before promotion; flip-report.ts reports the A/B flip; rollback-walker.ts implements versioned rollback; trace-summarize.ts compacts run telemetry for reflection. Together with the hooks from Step 8, these close the brainstorm → reflect → evolve → rollback loop.

tour.title: Optional MCP Servers
tour.description: Two optional stdio MCP servers extend Guild with durable memory and observability. guild-memory exposes BM25 search/read/list over the .guild/wiki/ knowledge base; guild-telemetry provides read-only structured query over .guild/runs/. They are wired in .mcp.json (Step 3) and consumed by context-assemble and reflect. This is where the project's narrative closes — the lifecycle now has persistent memory and a feedback signal.
tour.languageLesson: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers communicate over stdio with JSON-RPC. A read-only server like guild-telemetry exposes tools (trace_list_runs, trace_query) that the model calls — no network egress, the filesystem under .guild/ is the only data source.
